consequential_questions: Primary outcome and its unit (per plot or per plant)?
Number of entries/genotypes and whether all fit in one homogeneous block?
Locations and seasons; are the same entries at every location?
Is the treatment (e.g., irrigation) applied to whole plots or randomizable per plot?
Plot size, seed per entry, maximum plots per location?
Expected difference to detect and residual SD (pilot data or literature)?
Where are irrigation laterals, mains or sprinkler lines, and which way does water flow?
Known gradients: slope, drainage, previous crop, tree lines, roads, field edges?
Will you have border plots, and which rows of each plot are harvested?
Do entries differ a lot in height or maturity (neighbour competition)?
Can you record row and column for every plot (for spatial analysis)?
What is a pot/tray, and how many plants per pot?
Bench layout and known gradients (light, temperature, door, edges)?
Is measurement destructive or repeated on the same plant?
How is the treatment applied (per pot, per bench, per tray)?
Number of runs/batches over time?
Where are the door, cooling pads, fans, heaters and irrigation/sprinkler heads relative to the benches?
Will pots be rotated, or kept in fixed positions with blocks?
Pot size versus expected final plant size; pot colour?
How many chambers, and is the treatment a chamber setting (temperature, CO2, photoperiod)?
Can runs be repeated with treatments swapped between chambers?
Shelf/position effects inside each chamber?
Trays or flats: how many, how many cells each, and how is watering applied (per cell or per tray)?
Can a reference genotype go in every tray?
Has a uniformity pilot been run, and are independent sensors available?
Primary endpoint, expected effect and SD?
How is the treatment delivered (individual vs cage vs dam)?
Sex: factorial interest, or sex as a blocking factor?
Litter and cage structure; acquisition batches?
Repeated measurements and expected attrition/humane endpoints?
systems.disclaimer: Planning recommendation only; final designs require statistician, veterinarian and IACUC review.

consequential_questions: What is a biological replicate (plant, pool of plants, animal, culture)?
Conditions and time points; is sampling destructive?
Expected fold change of interest and sequencing depth?
Library prep and sequencing batches; can conditions be balanced across them?
systems.guidance: At least 6 biological replicates per condition; 12+ to capture most DE genes (Schurch et al. 2016, doi:10.1261/rna.053959.115).

consequential_questions: Biological replicate definition and how many per group?
Extraction and injection batches; can groups be balanced across batches?
Pooled QC frequency, blanks, and internal standards?
systems.guidance: Pooled QC at least every 10th injection, conditioning QCs at batch start (Broadhurst et al. 2018, doi:10.1007/s11306-018-1367-3).

consequential_questions: How many donors/animals per condition (the true n)?
Are conditions multiplexed or confounded with capture batch?
systems.guidance: Use pseudobulk per donor for differential expression (Squair et al. 2021, doi:10.1038/s41467-021-25960-2).

consequential_questions: Outcome (lifespan, fecundity, body size, behaviour) and whether the treatment is in the food/drug (vial is the unit) or genetic?
How are larval density and egg collection standardized?
Genetic background: backcross generations into which control stock? Wolbachia status?
Mated or virgin? Single-sex vials? Flies per vial and vials per treatment?
Food batch and incubator/tray layout?
systems.guidance: 100-150 flies per treatment as 10-15 per vial; backcross >=6 generations (Piper & Partridge 2016, doi:10.1007/978-1-4939-6371-3_18).

consequential_questions: What population: inbred panel, F2, RILs (SSD), NAM, backcross, diallel, North Carolina design, or sib-mated animal lines?
How many parents/founders, and how many generations of selfing or sib mating are planned?
Goal: estimate additive vs dominance variance (GCA/SCA), map QTL, or fix lines?
Pollination control: bagging, isolation distance, emasculation, outcrossing rate?
Seed source and maternal effects: are all parents grown in one environment before crossing?
systems.guidance: Inbreeding under selfing: F_t = 1 - (1/2)^t after t selfing generations (F6 ~ 0.97). Brother-sister mating needs ~20 generations for an inbred mouse strain (F ~ 0.986). (Falconer & Mackay 1996)

consequential_questions: Which environments (locations x years x managements), and are they chosen to represent the target population of environments?
Same entries in every environment, or partially overlapping sets?
Is the greenhouse/chamber trait meant to predict field performance? Which field trait and environments validate it?
Will environmental covariates (weather, soil, water input) be recorded for each environment?
systems.guidance: Analyse METs with a mixed model and factor-analytic GxE structure (Smith, Cullis & Thompson 2001); validate controlled-environment traits on independent field genotypes (Peirone et al. 2018).

consequential_questions: Which layers (GWAS, RNA-seq/eQTL, ATAC, Ribo-seq, metabolomics) and on the same individuals/tissue/time?
How many genotypes for the eQTL/GWAS part (power) vs how many replicates for the differential part?
Integration method: colocalization, TWAS, Mendelian randomization, or overlap of peaks and variants?
Are sampling date, time of day and tissue matched across layers?
systems.guidance: Correct GWAS for population structure and kinship (Q+K mixed model, Yu et al. 2006); integrate with colocalization or TWAS rather than nearest-gene overlap.

consequential_questions: Is matched RNA-seq from the same lysate planned (needed for translation efficiency)?
How will translation be arrested: flash freezing vs cycloheximide (initiation-site artifacts)?
Nuclease, footprint size window and rRNA depletion strategy for your organism?
Biological replicates per condition?
systems.guidance: Translation efficiency = footprints / mRNA, so matched RNA-seq is required; expect heavy rRNA contamination without depletion (Eastman et al. 2018; Ingolia et al. 2009).

consequential_questions: Tissue and nuclei isolation method (crude, FANS sorting, INTACT)?
Biological replicates (>= 2) and target depth?
In plants: expected chloroplast/mitochondrial read fraction and how you will reduce it?
Comparison design: conditions/genotypes, and matched RNA-seq?
systems.guidance: ENCODE: >=2 biological replicates, ~25M non-duplicate non-mito fragments, FRiP > 0.3, IDR reproducibility. Plants: crude nuclei gave ~50% organellar reads; FANS reduced it (Lu et al. 2017).

consequential_questions: What is the candidate evidence (GWAS hit, eQTL, ATAC peak) and how many candidates?
Validation route in each organism: CRISPR knockout, mutant alleles, overexpression, complementation, heterologous expression?
Are there at least two independent alleles/lines per gene and the right controls (empty vector, wild-type siblings, azygous segregants)?
In silico steps first: orthology, expression in the relevant tissue, colocalization, predicted variant effect?
systems.guidance: Validate with independent alleles and sibling controls; an in silico prediction prioritises but does not validate (design logic; Kaelin 2017 on validation pitfalls).

consequential_questions: How is the treatment given: in feed or water to a whole pen, cage or house (the pen is the unit) or to individual animals?
Animals per pen and pens per treatment; are pens blocked by room, barn position, litter or initial body weight?
Primary outcome (growth, feed efficiency, carcass, health score, microbiome) and its expected SD?
Where do the animals come from: litters, sires, farms or delivery batches? One breed or line?
Repeated measures over time, expected losses, and humane endpoints?
systems.reporting_checklist: ARRIVE 2.0; FASS Guide for the Care and Use of Agricultural Animals in Research and Teaching
systems.disclaimer: Planning recommendation only; final designs require statistician, veterinarian and animal care committee review.
systems.guidance: When diets or water treatments are given to pens, the pen is the experimental unit and n is the number of pens (Bello et al. 2016, J Dairy Sci 99:8871-8879, doi:10.3168/jds.2016-11516).
